learning_outcomes.text: describe fundamental natural science knowledge from physics and chemistry.
explain relevant connections in mechanical engineering based on this knowledge.
purposefully review the fundamentals of chemistry and physics.
apply application-oriented basic knowledge on selected mechanical engineering-related topics from physics to problems.
apply application-oriented basic knowledge on selected mechanical engineering-related topics from chemistry to problems.
adequately address simple questions from natural science fields in the context of engineering problems.
present work results in an audience-appropriate manner and summarize them concisely.
effectively plan work processes in laboratory and project contexts.
critically discuss and compare information from different sources.
systematically investigate risks, assumptions, and boundary conditions in projects.
discuss own solution proposals against the background of peer feedback.
purposefully use digital tools for research, analysis, and documentation.

syllabus_topics: Review of physical quantities and the SI unit system
Applications of acoustics and optics (measurement technology and material processing)
Selected chapters of modern physics (e.g., relativity theory, quantum physics, atomic and nuclear physics)
Chemistry of lubricants and additive chemistry
assessment_rules: Assessment for each course is carried out by a final exam, which can be either written or oral. The specific teaching and learning methods and examination modalities for each course are to be stated in the study and teaching information system before the start of the semester.
